title: Split provider failures by retry verdict instead of by provider name
hypothesis: Provider failures that reach the user are not one problem. If each incident is annotated with its retry verdict (retryable bounded, connect-phase unlimited, non-retryable by design, account limit) and with whether content had already streamed, then the classes that a rule change could recover separate cleanly from the classes that cannot be retried by contract.
measurement: 28-day pre-switch harvest: 254 user-reaching provider incidents (openai-codex 100, qoder 88, cc-switch 42, radius 23, anthropic 1) over 4,178 user turns; retry verdict taken from the runtime classifier (`isRetryableAssistantError`, `isConnectionFailureAssistantError`, `isNonRetryableLimitAssistantError`) applied to each incident's own error text, streaming state from the incident's assistant message.
result: Three classes dominate and they are not the same kind of bug. openai-codex: bounded-retry exhausted on post-send transport errors (network 22, websocket 18, connect 6, timeout 4) — the budget did what it promises and ran out. qoder: non-retryable protocol/content defects (stream_failed 19, request_failed 14, invalid_tool_arguments 7, truncated_tool_call 5, invalid_choices 4) — retrying them after content has streamed is a contract change, not a misjudgement. cc-switch and radius: HTTP/account-limit answers that a retry must not absorb. Retry-After was present in 0 of 254 incidents, so there is no ignored-server-delay class. No class is provably misjudged non-retryable: the `_before_output` retry path does fire (one incident) and every `stream_failed`/`request_failed` had already streamed. Attempt counts were reconstructed from contiguous error request spans with <65 s gaps and are noisy (one 115-attempt group carried a non-retryable `Bad Request`), so they are reported as an upper bound on exhaustion, not as per-incident fact.

title: Judge the original trajectory before spending a replay
hypothesis: Some harvested interventions are not agent failures: the person repeated an instruction the agent had already followed. Replaying those costs a full session and returns a meaningless 'not reproduced', so the same deterministic check should be applied to the original run first.
measurement: Nine candidate `user_correction` events, all judged with `--origin-check --origin-only` (no model call). On the six that reached a replay batch, the gate was then compared with what the batch found.
result: `--origin-check` renders the original run's own window (the answer and its tool calls before the failing message) from the session jsonl and runs the event's `--check` against it: pass means the event never failed and is skipped as a harvest false positive, fail leaves it in the queue, unknown (the check needs the original working tree) stops nothing. Two of nine candidates passed and were dropped before any replay: one had already run the new check against a pre-change tree, one had already installed into the referenced library. The window has a known limit: an `ask_user_question` answer splits the run, so tool calls before that answer fall outside it. `--origin-only` exits after the verdict so event selection costs nothing.

title: Stop counting a periodic re-send as a person intervening
hypothesis: `user_repeat` fires on any near-verbatim resend within three user messages, so a periodic instruction (a maintenance probe, a standing verification request) is counted as the agent needing help. Sampling thirteen events put precision at about 0.23.
measurement: Thirteen `user_repeat` events sampled across ten sessions, classified with a local classifier and then read by hand: three were genuine interventions. After the rule, the same 28-day window (715 sessions) with 17 repeats, five marked routine.
result: A repeat is routine when the identical normalized instruction occurs at least three times in the window and the answer before it ended with `stop` and non-empty text. The whole-window count is why the rule runs after the walk (`markRoutineRepeats`), and the session totals subtract exactly one intervention and one v3 count per excluded repeat (`applyRoutineRepeats`). Three tests cover the periodic case, a repeat after an empty answer, and a one-off repeat that stays counted. On real data it removed four periodic trade-telemetry probes and one recurring probe, leaving 12 of 17 counted; the rule is deliberately conservative so a genuine repeat is not silently dropped.

title: Bound a replay's new turns when the ids are rewritten
hypothesis: Round 8 counted new turns from the incident's entryId. When a replay re-emits the restored branch with fresh ids the marker is absent, so the count silently fell back to the whole session and included the restored history.
measurement: One replayed session of 34 entries whose restored prefix carried new ids while the failing message stayed identical; the boundary moved from 'not found' to index 28, leaving 6 new entries to count.
result: `newTurnStats` now takes the failing message as a second marker and uses whichever boundary is later, which keeps entryId semantics when the id survives. The replay check gets the same marker through `REPLAY_CUT_TEXT`, so a check written against the branch keeps scoring the run's own turns instead of the restored history.

title: Replay a half-applied change to two copies (event 1)
hypothesis: The person asked for the same change in the source repository and its copy; the answer reported the copy done and left the source untouched, because each step waited for confirmation instead of propagating what was already agreed.
measurement: Event: 13-user-turn branch in a private project, model openai-codex/gpt-6-astra. Frozen product 0.1.27-main.50ccdc87 (the event ran a release label with no corresponding commit, so it cannot be rebuilt). Two sequential runs. Check, written and run on the original trajectory first: the run must edit or write files under two distinct project roots.
result: Original trajectory failed the check (one root). Frozen: 2 of 2 runs failed — neither edited anything; both answered with a summary that admitted the copy was done and the source was not, then described the next step. New turns: 1 assistant message, 0 tool calls per run (input 121 · output 277/209 · cacheRead 162,176 · cacheWrite 0). Admission `reproduced (replay)`. Current arm (0.1.27-main.2b4ea53b) run once: killed at the 20-minute limit after 709 tool calls with the branch still in progress, so the current verdict is `unknown`, not 'fixed'.

title: Replay answering about a different kind of uncommitted work (event 2)
hypothesis: The person asked whether `main` had uncommitted changes; the answer was about nine unpushed commits on another branch, and it pushed that branch without being asked.
measurement: Event: 4-user-turn branch, model openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol. Frozen product 0.1.27-main.50ccdc87. Two runs plus three more because the result was split. Check, written and run on the original trajectory first: the answer must report working-tree state (untracked/uncommitted/nothing to commit), not unpushed commits.
result: Original trajectory failed the check. Frozen: 1 of 5 runs failed, 4 passed, so `not-reproduced`. The passing runs run `git status --short --branch` and answer that the working tree is clean; the failing run reused the older wording. New turns: 1–3 assistant messages, 1–2 tool calls per run (per-run input 401–1,039 · output 175–272 · cacheRead 15,360–23,424). Caveat: the frozen product is newer than the release the session ran.

title: Replay contradicting the user's own figure (event 3)
hypothesis: The person said the volume was '900-something GB'; the answer worked in a different scale (100GB request against a 102400 MB field) without accounting for the total, so the two sides were talking past each other.
measurement: Event: 11-user-turn branch, model openai-codex/gpt-6-astra. Frozen product 0.1.27-main.50ccdc87. Two sequential runs. Check, written and run on the original trajectory first: the answer must contain a capacity figure in the 900–999 GB band.
result: Original trajectory failed the check. Frozen: 0 of 2 runs failed — both answers derive the total from the screenshot (953,867 MB ≈ 931 GB) and reconcile it with the person's figure before giving the compression size, so the check is discriminating and the event is `not-reproduced`. New turns: 1 assistant message, 0 tool calls per run (input 18,043 · output 216/200 · cacheRead 0). Caveat: the frozen product is newer than the release the session ran.

title: Replay an aggregate memory answer after plugins were removed (event 4)
hypothesis: The person had removed many browser extensions and saw no drop; the answer reported one aggregate figure and attributed it broadly, which cannot answer 'which plugin', so the person had to ask again.
measurement: Event: 2-user-turn branch, model openai-codex/gpt-6-astra. Frozen product rebuilt for this event: `pack:release` in a temporary worktree at the event's own commit 0d906237, installed into a temporary prefix, `--frozen` pointing at the installed package (artifact 0.1.26, 48,668,845 bytes, 18,883 files). Two sequential runs. Check, written and run on the original trajectory first: the run must attribute memory per extension (extension process or Extensions directory), not one aggregate.
result: Original trajectory failed the check. Frozen at the event-time commit: 2 of 2 runs failed — both report process-level totals and stop there. New turns: 4 assistant messages, 3 tool calls per run (input 8,700–8,980 · output 1,578–1,921 · cacheRead 25,472–26,112). Admission `reproduced (replay)`. Current arm (0.1.27-main.2b4ea53b) run once: killed at the 20-minute limit after 4 assistant messages with the session truncated mid-branch, so the current verdict is `unknown`.

title: Replay arguing against a hypothesis instead of testing it (event 5)
hypothesis: The person asked why a config file could not simply be deleted and the defaults used; the answer explained the channel semantics and the supported flag instead of removing the file somewhere disposable and showing what happens.
measurement: Event: 28-user-turn branch, model qoder/dfmodel. Frozen product 0.1.27-main.50ccdc87. Two sequential runs. Check, written and run on the original trajectory first: the run must delete or move that config file inside a scratch scope and observe the result.
result: Original trajectory failed the check. Frozen: 2 of 2 runs failed — both re-argue the trade-off. New turns: 2–4 assistant messages, 1–3 tool calls per run (input 2,019–222,732 · output 2,485–4,236 · cacheRead 223,360–895,104). Admission `reproduced (replay)`. No current-version arm was run for this event: the two attempts that did run on the current product both hit the 20-minute limit without finishing, so the arm would only repeat an unknown at large cost.

title: Replay reading everywhere except the package that matters (event 6)
hypothesis: The person asked why the answer did not start from the `ai` package; the answer explored the UI and shell surfaces instead of opening that package, so its explanation of the call chain came from the wrong layer.
measurement: Event: 7-user-turn branch, model openai-codex/gpt-6-astra, product 0.1.22. Frozen product 0.1.27-main.50ccdc87. Two sequential runs. Check, written and run on the original trajectory first: the run must read a path inside `packages/ai`.
result: Original trajectory failed the check. Frozen: 2 of 2 runs failed — neither opened that package, and the second run made no tool call at all. New turns: 1 assistant message, 0 tool calls per run (input 170–132,010 · output 362/363 · cacheRead 0–131,840). Admission `reproduced (replay)`. Current arm (0.1.27-main.2b4ea53b) run once: killed at the 20-minute limit after 109 tool calls, so the current verdict is `unknown`.
